content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review:

- [Feature specification](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md)

Proposed scope: a private, single-user bookmark library supporting saving, editing, deletion, tags, notes, favorites, search, filtering, and sorting. Sharing, accounts, browser extensions, and import/export are excluded from the first release.

All specification quality checks pass, with no unresolved clarifications. Following the `speckit-specify` workflow, I’ve stopped before planning or implementation.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed.

Thanks — this reads well overall, and the scope you've drawn (saving, editing, deleting, tags, notes, favorites, search, filtering, sorting, and leaving out sharing/accounts/extensions/import-export for now) matches what I'm after for a first version.

One thing I want changed before I approve: the spec says I always have to type in the title myself when saving a link. That's not how I pictured it. The main reason I want this app is to save links quickly — usually I just have the web address. I'd expect that when I paste a link, the app fills in the page's name (and ideally a short description) for me automatically, and I can tweak it if I want. Having to hand-type a title every single time would make the everyday saving I care about most feel like a chore.

Could you fold that in — save by pasting the address, with the title (and description) pulled in automatically and still editable? The rest of the scope looks good to me.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for approval.

Key decisions:

- Single TypeScript application using React, Fastify, and SQLite.
- One production process on `0.0.0.0:4000`.
- Server-side metadata retrieval with redirect, timeout, response-size, and private-network protections following [OWASP SSRF guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html).
- Node’s built-in SQLite module, isolated behind a repository layer because it is currently designated release-candidate stability in the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/sqlite.html).
- Layered unit, integration, contract, desktop, and mobile tests.
- No accounts, sharing, extensions, import/export, or generated summaries.

Planning artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/data-model.md)
- [HTTP API contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

The OpenAPI contract passes validation. The `speckit-plan` workflow kept this phase limited to technical design; no application code or `tasks.md` has been created yet.

Please approve the plan or identify any changes. After approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

The plan matches what we agreed on, and it keeps things private and single-user like I wanted. The technical choices are your call — as long as the app does what the specification describes, I'm happy.

content:
The bookmark manager is built and ready for review at:

**http://maker:4000**

Implemented:

- Automatic editable title and description retrieval with safe fallback
- Persistent bookmark creation, editing, deletion, and duplicate confirmation
- Tags, notes, favorites, search, filtering, and sorting
- Responsive desktop/mobile interface with keyboard-accessible dialogs
- SSRF protections, bounded metadata fetching, and private SQLite storage
- Progressive rendering for libraries up to 10,000 bookmarks

Validation passed:

- Lint and strict type checking
- 13 unit, contract, and integration tests
- 7 desktop/mobile browser tests
- 10,000-bookmark update under one second
- Production build
- Zero known dependency vulnerabilities
- All 54 implementation tasks completed

Key artifacts:

- [Application source](/work/src/client/App.tsx)
- [Server entry point](/work/src/server/index.ts)
- [Completed tasks](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/tasks.md)
- [Validation results](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/validation-results.md)
- [Security validation](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/security-validation.md)

The `speckit-implement` workflow governed the phased build and completion checks. The review database starts empty.

I took it for a proper spin, and it does everything I was hoping for:

- I can save a page just by pasting its address — it pulls in the title (and a description when the page has one) automatically, and I can edit those before saving.
- My saved bookmarks stick around, and opening one takes me to the page.
- Tags, notes, and marking favorites all work, and I can edit or delete a bookmark (with a confirmation before it's gone).
- Searching finds pages by their title, address, notes, or tags regardless of capitalization, and filtering by a tag or favorites narrows things down.
- Sorting by newest, oldest, and title all behave as expected.
- Saving the same link again warns me and points to the one I already have instead of quietly duplicating it, and bad or non-web addresses are turned away with a clear message.

This is exactly the bookmark app I wanted. I'm happy with it — thank you.
